threads.thread_goal: Align on current routines, constraints, and select pilot group for the program.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Integrated Wellbeing Program for At-Risk Youth Group Home (project_pack_ref: Integrated Wellbeing Program for At-Risk Youth Group Home).
Goal for this thread: get a shared picture of current routines and agree on a small pilot group.

For T1 we need at least one full week of current routines mapped for each young person so we can later build A1.

Can you share:
- fixed times (school, therapy, contact visits)
- regular informal routines (gaming, gym, walks, chores)
- any time windows that are clearly not suitable for structured activities (e.g. typical crisis times)

Once we see the patterns, we will propose 5–7 youths for the first pilot group and confirm weekday time windows for activities.

@36599 and @87396, could you start with what you see on afternoon and early evening shifts?

From my last week of late shifts:
- School runs roughly 8:30–14:30 for most, two have vocational school blocks until 16:00 on Tue/Thu.
- Mon–Thu 15:00–17:00 is usually homework / decompressing. Some go straight to their rooms with headphones.
- 17:30–18:30 is dinner and kitchen chores.
- 19:00–21:00 is mostly gaming, TV, or short walks outside.

Typical hot spots where I would avoid new structured blocks:
- Right after school on Mondays (we often see conflicts then).
- Sunday evenings before school starts again.

For T1 I can start noting this systematically for each youth this week so we can fill A1 properly.

From my side on the days I am in:
- Two older youths have part-time work experience on Wed 16:00–19:00 every second week.
- One has therapy on Tue 15:30–16:30 and usually needs quiet time after.

I have noticed that 18:30–19:30 on Tue and Thu is often quite calm. That might be a possible slot later for vocational tasters, but we need to check clashes with existing routines once A1 is filled.

For T1 I can add notes on external appointments and work shifts.

Adding what I see on morning and day shifts:
- Breakfast and getting ready: 7:00–8:15, quite rushed.
- Some have individual sessions with external therapists during school hours; I will list those into T1 so we do not double-book.
- After school, 15:00–16:00, staff often support with homework or just listening if the day was rough.

I will start a simple table for T1 so we can later transfer into A1 without losing details.

On weekends:
- Saturday late morning is usually relaxed, some sleep in, some help with cleaning.
- Saturday afternoon we often go out (park, sports hall, shopping).
- Sunday afternoon is mixed: some want quiet, others get restless.

If we plan structured activities, I would suggest we focus on weekdays first and keep weekends more flexible, at least in the pilot.

For T1 I will document last weekend and the coming one so we see if this pattern holds.

Thanks all, this is helpful.

To move T1 forward, could we agree on a simple structure for A1:
- Rows: each youth
- Columns: weekday, school/therapy/work, typical mood after school, usual activities, clear no-go times, possible activity windows

@36599, can you draft that layout and share a quick screenshot or description here before we fill it, so we are consistent?

Yes, I can do that today.

I will set up A1 with:
- One tab per weekday
- Each row a youth
- Columns: fixed obligations, informal routines, typical mood, free slots, avoid slots

Then I will backfill last week from my notes for T1 and tag you when done so you can validate.

Great, thanks.

Next step in this thread is to shortlist youths for the pilot group.

My initial thought is to focus on those who:
- are currently in the home for at least the next school term
- have relatively stable school attendance
- have shown some interest in group activities or vocational topics

From my perspective, candidates could be: L, M, N, P, R, and S. That would be six youths.

@36599 and @87939, do you see any strong reasons to include or exclude someone from this list, especially considering trauma triggers or current crises?

On your list:
- L: fits well, usually engages if the group is not too big.
- M: I would include, but we should avoid late evenings because of sleep issues.
- N: currently in a more fragile phase after a family incident; I would suggest we wait with N for the first cycle.
- P: good candidate, often asks for more structured things to do.
- R: ok, but needs clear rules and predictable endings.
- S: I am unsure; S often refuses group offers but might join if there is a practical angle.

So I would propose we start with L, M, P, R, and maybe S if we keep the group size manageable and activities voluntary.

I agree with most of that.

Additional thoughts:
- N: I also feel it is better not to push new group structures right now.
- S: joins when there is food or something hands-on. If we include S, we should plan at least one activity that is clearly practical.

I would support starting with L, M, P, R, S as the pilot group, with the option to invite N later if things stabilise.

From a vocational angle:
- L and P have already asked about work and training.
- R likes anything with tools.
- S has joined cooking a few times.

So the proposed group L, M, P, R, S makes sense to me. For M we just need to avoid late slots as mentioned.

Thanks for the input.

Unless anyone objects by tomorrow noon, we will confirm the first pilot group as youths L, M, P, R, and S.

We will keep N in mind for a later cycle once things are calmer.

Next, we should pin down weekday time windows that are realistic for structured activities, based on what we are already entering into A1 for T1.

Looking at the patterns we described so far, I would suggest these possible weekday windows for structured activities:
- Mon–Thu: 16:30–17:30 (after initial decompression, before dinner)
- Tue and Thu: 18:30–19:30 (for those who are ok with something after dinner)

I would avoid:
- Monday 15:00–16:00
- Any slot after 20:00

We can still keep flexibility for individual needs, but this gives us a base to plan T3 later.

I can work with those windows.

For M specifically, I would prefer the 16:30–17:30 slot rather than after dinner, to protect sleep.

For S, the 18:30–19:30 slot might be better on days when there is a cooking or practical activity, because S often hangs around the kitchen then.

For future vocational tasters, the Tue/Thu 18:30–19:30 slot sounds good, especially for short, hands-on sessions.

I will keep that in mind when I work on T5 and A6, but we can adjust if school or therapy changes.

I agree with the proposed windows.

One small note: on Wednesdays we sometimes have unplanned meetings with external workers around 16:00–17:00. I will add those into T1 as they come up so we can see in A1 if a specific day becomes too crowded.

But as a general rule, 16:30–17:30 and 18:30–19:30 on Tue/Thu look workable.

Summarising where we are:
- Proposed pilot youths: L, M, P, R, S.
- Main weekday activity windows: Mon–Thu 16:30–17:30, plus Tue/Thu 18:30–19:30 for those who want an extra session.

If there are no objections by tomorrow noon, I will treat this as agreed and use it as the basis for T3 and the first version of A5.

Please react with a thumbs up if you are ok with this plan.
Thumbs up from me. The group and time windows sound realistic from the floor perspective.
Also ok for me. I will plan vocational ideas around those slots so we do not overload the youths.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the weekly structured activity schedule and co-designed activities.

messages.text:
As a follow-up to our alignment on routines and the pilot group, I am sharing the first draft of the weekly structured activity schedule for the pilot youths L, M, P, R, S.

Based on A1 and the agreed time windows (from T1 and TH1), I have drafted A5 and a first version of T3 with these blocks:
- Mon–Thu 16:30–17:30: core wellbeing / social skills / homework support blocks.
- Tue and Thu 18:30–19:30: optional practical or vocational tasters.

We also need to integrate at least two co-designed activities for T6.

Please share comments on:
1) Is the balance between structure and free time ok?
2) Which youth ideas we should prioritise as co-designed activities?

Once we converge, we will confirm the initial schedule (D3) and select the co-designed activities (D4).

Thanks for pulling this together.

From the youth discussions I had for T6, the main ideas were:
- Cooking club once a week (they suggested simple meals and snacks).
- Music / creative corner (beats, drawing, maybe some digital art).
- Short outdoor challenge (walk with a small goal, like taking photos or a scavenger list).

I have started documenting two of these in T6 with goals and simple rules. For A5, I would suggest:
- Tue 18:30–19:30: cooking club (co-designed).
- Thu 18:30–19:30: rotating creative corner (co-designed).

We could keep the outdoor challenge as a flexible option for one of the 16:30–17:30 slots when the weather is good.

Looking at the draft A5, I like the idea of using the later slots for practical things.

For the Tue cooking club, I can link it with basic kitchen skills from T5 later (like safe knife use, hygiene) without making it feel like a class.

For Thu creative corner, I can support with simple CV or future-dreams exercises now and then, but I would not put that in every week so it stays fun.

On the 16:30–17:30 blocks, the draft shows:
- Mon: check-in circle and planning the week.
- Tue: homework support and quiet focus.
- Wed: social skills / group game.
- Thu: wellbeing topic (sleep, stress, feelings) with a light format.

From the floor, this seems manageable if we keep the content simple and avoid heavy trauma topics in the group. For more sensitive issues we should stick to one-to-one or follow the crisis guide later (A3) when it is ready.

I like the cooking club and creative corner as the two main co-designed activities.

From what the youths told me, they value:
- having a say in the menu or theme
- being able to opt out without pressure

So in T6 we should write the rules clearly: voluntary, clear start and end, and a short check-out at the end.

For A5, I support placing them exactly where you suggested: Tue and Thu 18:30–19:30.

Good suggestions.

To make sure we do not overload certain days:
- Mon 16:30–17:30: check-in circle and light planning.
- Tue 16:30–17:30: homework / quiet focus.
- Tue 18:30–19:30: co-designed cooking club.
- Wed 16:30–17:30: social skills / group game.
- Thu 16:30–17:30: wellbeing topic in a gentle format.
- Thu 18:30–19:30: co-designed creative corner.

Does anyone see a conflict with school, therapy, or typical crisis times for L, M, P, R, S based on A1?

For M, the only concern is not going too late. With this plan, M can join the Tue cooking club occasionally but we should not expect every week.

For S, the Tue cooking slot is actually perfect; S is often around the kitchen then.

I do not see major clashes with A1. We just need to be ready to skip a session if there was a big incident that day.

Agree with @36599. The only recurring external appointment that might touch these times is N's therapy, but N is not in the first pilot group.

For L and P, the schedule looks fine. R might need a clear explanation that participation is voluntary but that we expect basic respect for the group rules when present.

I suggest we add a short group agreement to T3 and A5 so all staff present use the same wording.

From my side, I can be present for most Tue and Thu evening slots.

For the Wed social skills block, I might not always be there, so it would be good if the plan in T3 includes simple games that any staff can run without special training.

One small suggestion: on Mon check-in, we could also ask the youths which of the co-designed activities they want to focus on that week (for example, type of dish or creative theme). That keeps the participation element strong.

I can add a short prompt for that into T6 and A5.

That is a good idea.

To move towards closure: can we confirm that the two main co-designed activities for this pilot are:
1) Cooking club on Tue 18:30–19:30.
2) Creative corner on Thu 18:30–19:30.

The outdoor challenge will stay as a flexible option for one of the 16:30–17:30 slots when conditions allow.

If you agree, please react or reply so we can record this as our selection for D4.
Yes, I confirm those two as the co-designed activities. The youths were most excited about exactly these ideas.
Confirmed from my side as well. Cooking club and creative corner as the two fixed co-designed activities, with outdoor challenge as an occasional add-on.

Thanks everyone.

Given the feedback and no objections, I propose we formally approve this initial weekly structured activity schedule in A5 for the pilot group (D3), with:
- Mon–Thu 16:30–17:30 core blocks as described.
- Tue and Thu 18:30–19:30 as the two co-designed activities.

I will finalise T3 accordingly and share the updated A5 with the group home manager for sign-off.

If anyone has last-minute concerns, please share them today; otherwise I will treat D3 and D4 as agreed.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on templates and tools: individual plans, handover checklist, and monitoring log.

messages.text:
I have uploaded first drafts of our key tools:
- A2: Individual Support and Development Plan Template (for T2).
- A4: Shift Handover and Coordination Checklist (for T7).
- A7: Wellbeing and Engagement Monitoring Log (for T8).

In this thread, I would like quick feedback on:
1) Is the language clear enough for all shifts?
2) Are we missing any essential information for handovers?
3) Are the monitoring indicators simple but useful?

Once we adjust, we will approve the individual plan template (D5) and agree on the final checklist and indicators (D6).

On A2:
- I like that each plan starts with the youths own goals in their words.
- The sections on wellbeing, social skills, education, and risks are clear.

Maybe we could add a small box for 'what helps when I am upset' so staff can see preferred calming strategies quickly.

On A4:
- The checklist covers mood, incidents, appointments, and plan updates. That is good.
- Could we add a line for 'who had a positive moment today' so we do not only pass on problems?

I went through A2 and A7.

For A2:
- The risk indicators section is useful, but we should keep the wording neutral so it does not feel like labelling. Maybe use 'things to watch out for' instead of 'risk factors'.

For A7:
- The four indicators you propose (participation, mood, conflicts, and engagement with activities) seem manageable.
- The 0–3 scale is simple, but we should give one example per number so staff rate similarly.

I can help draft those examples into T8.

From my perspective, A4 is very helpful. I often come in and do not know what happened the day before.

One question: in A7, should we also note if a youth joined a vocational taster specifically, or is that included under general participation? I am fine either way, but I want to be sure I fill it correctly.

I like the structure overall.

On A4, I would add a small reminder to check the crisis and trauma-support guide (A3) if there was a serious incident, so that follow-up steps are not forgotten.

On A7, maybe we can keep vocational participation as a short note in the comments column, so we do not add more indicators but still see patterns.

Thanks for the concrete suggestions.

I will adjust A2 to:
- Add a box 'what helps when I am upset'.
- Rename 'risk factors' to 'things to watch out for'.

For A4, I will add:
- A line for 'positive moments to share'.
- A reminder to check A3 if there was a crisis.

For A7, I will keep the four indicators and add short examples for each level in T8, and note that vocational participation can be mentioned in the comments field.

Those changes sound good to me.

With the extra calming-strategies box and the positive-moments line, I feel A2 and A4 will be very usable on busy shifts.

I am ok with using the comments field in A7 to note vocational participation.

The 0–3 examples will help me a lot, because I sometimes struggle to decide between two numbers.

Once you have updated A2, I am ready to start using it with the pilot youths.

For A7, I suggest we start with daily ratings during the first two weeks of the pilot, then review in T11 if that is sustainable or if we should move to every second day.

Great.

Before we formally approve, can you confirm:
- A2: ok to use as the standard individual plan template for the pilot?
- A4: ok as the handover checklist for all shifts?
- A7: ok with the four indicators and 0–3 scale plus examples, with daily ratings in the first two weeks?

If yes, we will record D5 for A2 and D6 for A4 and A7.
From my side: yes to all three. They are clear and not too heavy.
I also agree. A2, A4, and A7 are ready to use in the pilot as described.

Thanks for confirming.

We will treat A2 as the approved individual plan template (D5) and A4 plus A7 as the agreed handover checklist and monitoring indicators (D6).

I will finalise T2, T7, and T8 accordingly and share a short how-to in the next briefing thread.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate vocational skills taster modules within the weekly schedule.

messages.text:
I have drafted proposals for the vocational skills taster modules for T5 and added them into A6.

The four short modules are:
1) Basic cooking and kitchen safety (linked to the Tue cooking club).
2) Everyday money and budgeting.
3) Simple DIY and tool use.
4) First steps in job search (interests, strengths, and simple CV basics).

Each module has objectives, duration (45–60 minutes), and required materials in A6.

We need to:
- Decide which modules to run in the first pilot cycle (D7).
- Agree on days and times that fit with A5 and do not clash with school or therapy (D8).

My initial thought is to use the Tue and Thu 18:30–19:30 slots from A5 and rotate modules there, but I want to check feasibility with you first.

Thanks for putting A6 together.

Given the pilot group and our focus on keeping things light, I would prioritise:
- Basic cooking and kitchen safety.
- Simple DIY and tool use.
- First steps in job search.

Everyday money is important, but it might be a bit abstract for some of the younger ones right now. Maybe we can bring it in the next cycle.

On timing, Tue and Thu 18:30–19:30 are our co-designed activity slots in A5. We need to be careful not to turn those into formal lessons. Maybe we can weave the vocational elements into those sessions instead of adding separate blocks.

From the youths comments, they are more open to practical things than to anything that feels like school.

So I agree with focusing on cooking, DIY, and a very light version of job search.

For timing, I would suggest:
- Use Tue cooking club for the cooking module content.
- Use Thu creative corner sometimes for DIY (for example, small repair or craft projects).
- For job search basics, maybe use one or two Mon check-ins or Wed social skills blocks, but keep it short and mixed with other activities.

I would avoid adding extra separate sessions beyond what is already in A5, at least in the first weeks.

I agree with the others.

If we integrate the vocational modules into existing A5 slots, we reduce the risk of clashes with school and therapy and keep the routine predictable.

For D8, I would propose:
- Tue 18:30–19:30: cooking module elements.
- Thu 18:30–19:30: DIY elements on some weeks, creative on others.
- One Wed 16:30–17:30 per month: light job search / future talk.

We can then record in T9 which module content was actually delivered in each session.

This structure sounds realistic.

For the job search module, I would keep it very exploratory: talking about what they enjoy, what they are good at, maybe looking at pictures of different jobs, rather than writing full CVs.

We can still note in A6 that the module can be adapted by age and interest.

Thanks, that helps.

So for D7, are we saying that the first pilot cycle will include these three modules from A6:
1) Basic cooking and kitchen safety.
2) Simple DIY and tool use.
3) First steps in job search.

And for D8, the agreed times are:
- Tue 18:30–19:30 (cooking content).
- Thu 18:30–19:30 (DIY or creative with vocational flavour).
- One Wed 16:30–17:30 per month (future / job talk).

If that is correct, I will update T5 and A6 to reflect that and prepare T9 for the pilot sessions.

Yes, that matches my understanding.

I would just add that we keep the option to adjust the frequency of the Wed future / job talk if we see that it is too much or too little in the monitoring data in A7 and the feedback summary in A8 later.

I confirm the three modules and the timing as you summarised.

From the floor, I think this is a good balance between practical skills and not overloading the evenings.

Same here: I agree with the three modules and the proposed times.

We can always fine-tune after the first few weeks when we look at T11 and T12.

Great, thanks for the confirmations.

I will treat D7 and D8 as agreed:
- Modules: cooking, DIY, and first steps in job search.
- Times: Tue and Thu 18:30–19:30 plus one Wed 16:30–17:30 per month.

Next I will finalise A6 and prepare a simple attendance and feedback sheet for T9 so we can capture what works for the youths.

threads.thread_goal: Review first two weeks of pilot, discuss incidents, and agree on adjustments.

messages.text:
We have now completed the first two weeks of the pilot.

I have summarised feedback from youths and staff into A8 for T11 and looked at the early trends in A7.

Key points from A8:
- Participation: L, P, and R attend most sessions; M joins mainly earlier ones; S joins cooking and some DIY.
- Mood: slight improvement on Mon check-ins; some tension on Thu when the day at school was heavy.
- Co-designed activities: cooking club is very popular; creative corner is mixed, depending on the theme.
- Vocational tasters: basic cooking elements worked well; DIY was ok but needed more structure.
- Incidents: one escalation after a conflict on gaming rules; we followed A3 and the handover in A4 captured it well.

In this thread, we should:
- Decide whether to keep the same pilot group or adjust it (D1).
- Decide which co-designed activities to keep, modify, or replace (D4).
- Identify 2–3 concrete adjustments for T12.

Please share your observations from shifts and any suggestions for changes.

From my late shifts:
- Cooking club: all five youths showed up at least once; they liked choosing the menu.
- Creative corner: L and P engaged, R sometimes disrupted when bored, S only joined when there was music.
- Wed social skills: went well when we used games; less so when we tried more talking.

On the incident: R and S argued about game time before the Wed session. We used the de-escalation steps from A3 and noted it in A4. The next day, mood scores in A7 were lower but back to baseline after two days.

I think the pilot group composition is ok; I would not add or remove anyone yet.

On morning and day shifts, I noticed:
- L seems to look forward to Mon check-ins and mentions them in the morning.
- M is more settled on days after a good homework session.
- S is proud when something from cooking turns out well and talks about it.

Looking at A7, participation scores are highest on Mon and Tue, a bit lower on Thu.

I agree with keeping the same pilot group for now. For co-designed activities, I would keep cooking as is, and adjust creative corner to include more music and maybe some simple digital art, as the youths suggested in feedback for T11.

From the vocational side:
- Cooking module elements worked smoothly; youths picked up hygiene and basic skills without it feeling like a lesson.
- DIY session was a bit chaotic; we had too many tools out at once and not enough clear steps.
- The short future talk we tried on Wed was ok for L and P, but R and S lost interest quickly.

For adjustments, I suggest:
- Break DIY into smaller tasks with clear roles.
- Keep future talks very short and maybe one-to-one for those who want more.

I do not see a need to change the pilot group.

I agree with the others: the group seems right.

On co-designed activities:
- Cooking: keep as is, maybe add a simple feedback question at the end (what should we cook next time?).
- Creative corner: I would rename it to 'music and creative corner' and plan at least one music-related option each time.

For T12 adjustments, I would propose:
1) Shorten Thu wellbeing talk and add a small game at the end.
2) Add a fixed 5-minute closing round to all sessions to check how everyone is leaving.
3) Simplify the DIY module steps in A6.

Thanks for the detailed observations.

On the pilot group (D1):
- I hear a clear message to keep L, M, P, R, S in the group and not add or remove anyone right now.

On co-designed activities (D4):
- Cooking club: keep as is, with a small end-of-session feedback question.
- Creative corner: adjust to 'music and creative corner' with more music and digital options.

On concrete adjustments for T12, I propose we agree on these three:
1) Shorten Thu wellbeing talk and end with a light game.
2) Add a 5-minute closing round to all structured sessions.
3) Simplify DIY steps in A6 and limit the number of tools out at once.

Please confirm or suggest changes before we lock this in.

I agree with all three adjustments and with keeping the same pilot group.

The closing round will also help us notice if someone leaves more upset than they show during the activity.

Confirmed from my side as well:
- Same pilot group.
- Cooking club unchanged, creative corner adjusted towards music.
- Three adjustments for T12 as you listed.

I will also remind staff in handovers (A4) to note if the closing round brings up anything that needs follow-up.

I am on board with this.

I will rework the DIY part in A6 to have fewer steps and clearer roles, and I will build the closing round question into my session plans.

Same here: I support keeping the group and adjusting creative corner and the three points for T12.

I can help collect short youth quotes about what they like in cooking and music for the next A8 update.

Thanks everyone.

We will record:
- D1: pilot group remains L, M, P, R, S for the next phase.
- D4: we keep cooking club and adjust creative corner into 'music and creative corner', with the outdoor challenge remaining a flexible option.

I will update A5 and A6 and implement the three agreed adjustments in T12, then reflect them in the next version of A8 after the following two weeks.

Please continue to use A7 daily for now so we can see if these changes have an effect.
